phase: Monetary Policy Reaction Function — Measurement Source Screening
purpose: Determine whether Romania has exact, frequency-compatible and semantically defensible inflation-gap, activity-gap and expectations observables for a policy reaction function without converting qualitative survey balances or model-based gaps into observed shocks.

inflation_target.role: Allows an observed inflation-target midpoint for an inflation-gap measurement contract.

consumer_price_expectations.institution: European Commission DG ECFIN / Eurostat BCS
consumer_price_expectations.concept: Consumer qualitative balance: price trends over the next 12 months
consumer_price_expectations.semantic_limit: A balance of survey responses is not an expected annual inflation rate in percentage points and cannot be subtracted from the BNR target as if units matched.
consumer_price_expectations.romania_revision_note: Romania consumer survey publication resumed in April 2024; consistent monthly/quarterly balances were restored using new data from May 2023 and econometric techniques. Disaggregate category/share results were not restored consistently.

evidence: BNR/NBR publications display a quantitative financial-analyst survey with 1-year-ahead and 2-year-ahead inflation expectations in percent.
A March-2023 NBR presentation shows quarterly history through 2022-Q4 plus January-February 2023 observations.
Historical BNR research notes that charted expectations can be shifted to the period to which they refer, rather than plotted at the date when they were formed.
financial_analyst_expectations.semantic_limit: The quantitative concept is unit-compatible with percentage inflation, but charts/presentations do not constitute an immutable formation-date dataset. The historical display convention may shift observations to target horizon, so direct chart extraction would risk look-ahead misdating.
financial_analyst_expectations.horizon_mapping_boundary: A policy reaction function requires expectations indexed by the information/formation date available to policymakers. Horizon-shifted chart coordinates are not a formation-time vintage and may not be read as such.

bnr_inflation_forecast.semantic_limit: Central-bank forecast is part of the policy information set/model and is not interchangeable with private-sector expectations; using it in a policy rule would require explicit simultaneity/model-consistency treatment.

activity_gap_ameco.dataset: AMECO potential-output related variables including AVGDGP/OVGDP
activity_gap_ameco.semantic_limit: Annual model-based output gap is not a quarterly observed activity gap and may be revised with forecast vintages.

activity_gap_bnr.concept: GDP/aggregate-demand gap used in Inflation Reports
activity_gap_bnr.semantic_limit: The gap is a model-based real-time policy-information variable, not directly observed output. A policy-rule dataset must retain report/decision vintages and map each estimate to the information set available at the policy decision date; a later revised path may not be backfilled as if known in real time.
evidence: BNR Inflation Reports publish a quarterly GDP gap path in percent of potential GDP.
The November-2024 Inflation Report states that the macro projection used information available through 29 October 2024.
The same report compares the current GDP-gap assessment with the previous forecast round, demonstrating vintage/revision dependence.

prohibited_shortcuts: Do not interpret the CONS_006 qualitative balance as percentage inflation expectations.
Do not use BNR staff inflation forecasts as private expectations without an explicit structural information-set contract.
Do not interpolate annual AMECO output gaps to quarters and call them observed quarterly gaps.
Do not estimate a Taylor-type rule on full-sample revised gaps without real-time-vintage treatment.
Do not treat observed exchange-rate movements as exogenous policy-rule regressors in a managed-float regime.
Do not activate the monetary-credit feedback merely because target and policy-rate histories are observed.
Do not digitise the financial-analyst expectations chart or treat target-horizon-shifted chart positions as survey formation dates.
Do not digitise the BNR GDP-gap chart into a pseudo real-time series.
Do not backfill later revised BNR GDP-gap estimates into earlier policy-decision information sets.
reopen_trigger: Retain a machine-readable quantitative financial-analyst expectations history indexed by survey formation date (or a reproducible source preserving that mapping); retain quarterly BNR activity-gap vintages with information cutoffs/revision timing; then freeze policy-regime/intervention and simultaneity identification before any reaction-function fit.
